items.followUp: Define Inorganic Chemistry and name two industries in which it is applied.

rubric.why: This earns the definition mark by identifying the subject matter of organic chemistry.
rubric.description: Defines organic chemistry as the study of hydrocarbons and their derivatives, or carbon compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: This earns the mark for naming two relevant industries.
rubric.description: Names two industries covered by organic chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two relevant industries.

modelAnswer: Organic chemistry is the branch of chemistry that studies hydrocarbons and their derivatives.
It is used in industries such as the pharmaceutical and plastic industries.

items.followUp: Explain why atomic size increases down a group in the periodic table.

rubric.why: A greater nuclear charge across a period is the cause of the increased attraction for electrons.
rubric.description: States that nuclear charge increases across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the increase in nuclear charge.

rubric.why: This links the increased nuclear attraction to the decrease in atomic size.
rubric.description: Explains that added electrons enter the same shell, so shielding changes little and the stronger attraction pulls electrons closer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the effect on electron attraction or atomic size.

modelAnswer: Across a period, the nuclear charge increases because the number of protons increases.
The added electrons enter the same shell, so shielding changes little; the stronger attraction pulls the electrons closer to the nucleus and atomic size decreases.

items.followUp: Why is the third ionization energy of an element higher than its second ionization energy?

rubric.why: The second electron is removed from a positively charged ion, not from a neutral atom.
rubric.description: States that the second electron is removed from an already positive ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the positive ion.

rubric.why: The remaining electrons experience stronger attraction, making the next electron harder to remove.
rubric.description: Explains that the ion holds its remaining electrons more strongly after losing the first electron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the stronger attraction or increased difficulty of removal.

modelAnswer: After the first electron is removed, the atom becomes a positive ion.
The remaining electrons are attracted more strongly to the nucleus, so more energy is needed to remove the second electron than the first.

items.followUp: Define an ionic bond and give one example.

rubric.why: Sharing electron pairs is the defining feature of a covalent bond.
rubric.description: Defines a covalent bond as a bond formed by sharing electron pairs between atoms.

rubric.why: A valid example demonstrates the definition.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of a covalent substance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is a chemical bond formed when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
For example, the bond between the two hydrogen atoms in H₂ is covalent.

items.followUp: Name four factors that affect the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: These are accepted factors affecting diffusion; the first two correctly identified factors earn the first mark.
rubric.description: Names two correct factors affecting diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct factors.

rubric.why: The question requires four factors, so two further correct factors earn the second mark.
rubric.description: Names two additional correct factors, for four in total.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when four distinct correct factors are named.

modelAnswer: Four factors that affect diffusion are temperature, concentration gradient, particle size and the nature of the medium.

rubric.why: A boiling point is a temperature, so this is an essential part of the definition.
rubric.description: Identifies boiling point as a temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a temperature.

rubric.why: This specifies the change or condition that occurs at the boiling point.
rubric.description: States that a liquid boils and changes into gas, or that its vapour pressure equals the external pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the boiling/change-of-state condition or the vapour-pressure condition.

modelAnswer: The boiling point is the temperature at which a liquid boils and changes into a gas.
At this temperature, the vapour pressure of the liquid equals the external atmospheric pressure.

items.followUp: Name four metals that are highly reactive.

rubric.why: Any two of the listed least-reactive or noble metals earn the first mark.
rubric.description: Names two correct noble or least-reactive metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct metals.

rubric.why: Two further correct metals complete the requested list of four.
rubric.description: Names two further correct noble or least-reactive metals, for four in total.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for all four distinct correct metals.

modelAnswer: Four noble or least-reactive metals are gold, silver, platinum and copper.

items.followUp: Define a saturated solution and give one example.

rubric.why: An aqueous solution is specifically a solution whose solvent is water.
rubric.description: Defines an aqueous solution as one in which water is the solvent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that water is the solvent.

rubric.why: A correct example illustrates an aqueous solution.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example, such as salt or sugar dissolved in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

modelAnswer: An aqueous solution is a solution in which water is the solvent.
For example, sodium chloride dissolved in water forms an aqueous solution.
